our code executes|application runs the tool|code calls the API
result goes back|tool result returned|send result back
step cap|max steps|iteration limit
timeout per call|deadline|budget

narration.text: A customer asks why parcel 4471 is late. The model has two tools: track a parcel, and open a support case.
The model can't run anything itself. It replies with a request to call the tracking tool for parcel 4471.
Our code checks that the parcel belongs to this customer, then calls the tracking service.
The first call times out. Here's the decision point: a read is safe to repeat, so our code retries it once after a short wait.
Had that failed too, we'd send back a result marked as an error, saying the service is slow. This time it works: a weather hold at the depot.
With that result, the model writes its answer instead of asking for another tool, so the loop ends.
If it had kept asking for tools, our cap of eight steps would have stopped the run and passed the case to a person.
Before the reply goes out, our code checks that it matches the tracking result we actually received.
